newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CALM IN S.AFRICA'S ZULU REGION AIDS WAR ON CRIME.
newsitem.headline: CALM IN S.AFRICA'S ZULU REGION AIDS WAR ON CRIME.

text.p: A steady fall in political killings has boosted the fight of South African police against violent crime in KwaZulu-Natal province, a spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The decrease in the number of politically motivated incidents since the local government elections has enabled (us) to...focus attention on fighting crime," Director Bala Naidoo said in a statement.
President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) and its rival Zulu-based Inkatha agreed on peace pacts before the June municipal polls to try end years of bloodshed.
It still takes its toll but on a much reduced scale.
Naidoo said provincial police recovered 2,000 firearms so far this year, including notorious Russian-made AK-47s. Most guns are smuggled in from Mozambique.
"The smuggling of weapons through our province is still a big problem," Naidoo told Reuters.
He said house searches, patrols and roadblocks also led to the arrest of 7,133 people for crimes including murder, rape and theft over the same period.
